The day can only introduce each layer of the toolchain, and the [companion curriculum](../../companion/index.qmd) takes each one further.

| If you want | Read |
|---|---|
| The rest of R, from the first line to a figure of your own | [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd) |
| The IDE in depth, and the differences between the three | [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd) |
| The document format in full: the header, chunk options, figures, tables, cross-references and citations | [Quarto and reproducible documents](../../companion/quarto.qmd) |
| Version control from first principles, and a repository of your own online | [Git and GitHub](../../companion/git-github.qmd) |
| To turn your own GESIS downloads into the respondent file, the scales and the panel | [Building the analysis file](../../companion/data-management.qmd) |
| Where the data come from: the archives, survey programmes and statistical offices, and the sources of this case step by step | [Social science data sources](../../companion/data-sources.qmd) |
| Where finished work is deposited, what a licence allows others to do with it, and the preregistration templates | [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) |
| The statistics behind the three models that you reproduced | [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd), sections 1 to 5 |

The other formats of the course take the same case in other directions: the [open-science day](../eu-frames-one-day-open-science/index.qmd) gives the time of this day to the practices of open research and to replication, the [methods day](../eu-frames-one-day-methods/index.qmd) gives it to the statistics and to the menu of alternative analyses, and the [three-day course](../eu-frames-three-days/index.qmd) builds the data from the raw survey files and reproduces all five analysts.
